advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the httpx2 module resolution (importorskip) inside the `else`/non-bedrock branch of test_provider_parity `_capture` so bedrock cases are never skipped for a missing httpx2.
evidence: tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:656: `    anthropic_http = _anthropic_transport_http_module()`
tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:653: `            return pytest.importorskip("httpx2")`
tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:677: `    if bedrock:` — bedrock path never uses `anthropic_http`
The importorskip runs for every model, so a missing httpx2 skips the bedrock parity assertions too.
advisory.finding: In test_provider_parity `_capture`, `anthropic_http = _anthropic_transport_http_module()` (which calls `pytest.importorskip("httpx2")` when the installed anthropic SDK expects httpx2) runs UNCONDITIONALLY, before the `if bedrock:` branch. For bedrock models — which never touch the anthropic http client — this makes the parity test skip whenever the SDK expects httpx2 but httpx2 is not importable, silently dropping bedrock parity coverage that has nothing to do with httpx2.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute `anthropic_http` only in the non-bedrock branch (right before the `monkeypatch.setattr(anthropic_http, "AsyncHTTPTransport", ...)` call).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the `inspect.signature(...)` calls in `_move_unsupported_beta_create_kwargs`/`_anthropic_http_client_module` so an introspection failure degrades gracefully instead of aborting provider construction.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:182: `    params = inspect.signature(create).parameters`
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:112: `    http_client = inspect.signature(async_anthropic_cls.__init__).parameters.get("http_client")`
Neither call is wrapped in try/except; an introspection failure propagates out of `_build_retrying_anthropic_provider`.
advisory.finding: `_move_unsupported_beta_create_kwargs` and `_anthropic_http_client_module` call `inspect.signature(...)` on the SDK's `create`/`__init__` without catching `ValueError`/`TypeError`. If a future SDK exposes these as a non-introspectable callable (C-accelerated, functools.partial without __wrapped__, or a builtin), `inspect.signature` raises and aborts the entire provider construction, rather than degrading gracefully.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `_build_retry_wait` test that supplies a VALID FUTURE HTTP-date `Retry-After` and asserts the returned wait equals the computed seconds-until-that-date (capped at max_wait), not the jittered fallback.
evidence: Added logic honoring a future HTTP-date: `retry_time = parsedate_to_datetime(retry_after)` ... `wait_seconds = (retry_time - datetime.now(timezone.utc)).total_seconds()` ... `if wait_seconds <= 0: return None` ... `return min(wait_seconds, max_wait)` (anthropic_model.py:95-104)

tests/unit/test_transport_retry_jitter.py:131 `test_expired_http_date_retry_after_falls_to_jittered_fallback` covers only an EXPIRED date; `test_positive_retry_after_is_honored_and_capped` (line 144) uses only an INTEGER header ('5','999').
ABSENCE: no test passes a `Retry-After: <future RFC-1123 date>` and asserts the returned wait equals the computed positive seconds-until-that-date (capped at max_wait).
advisory.finding: The newly-added `_retry_after_delay` honors a VALID FUTURE HTTP-date `Retry-After` by computing a positive wait (min(wait_seconds, max_wait)), but no test drives that input — the jitter suite only asserts integer-positive Retry-After and an EXPIRED HTTP-date (which falls to the fallback). A regression that mis-parses or drops a future HTTP-date (e.g. returning None and collapsing to the jittered fallback instead of honoring the server's date) would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_transport_retry_jitter.py, add: build a header via `format_datetime(datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=30), usegmt=True)`, then assert `0 < wait(state) <= 30` (and, with a large max_wait, that it is close to 30) — mirroring `test_expired_http_date_retry_after_falls_to_jittered_fallback` but for the honored branch.
